points.description: States that nonlinearly transforming the features lets the model/classifier learn or represent complex (non-linear) data patterns, e.g. make non-linearly separable classes separable.
points.partial_credit: Half if only vaguely says it improves classification or handles data better, without mentioning complex/non-linear patterns or separability.

points.description: States that with nonlinear features even simple/basic (linear) classifiers such as SVM can classify complex data sets efficiently and effectively.
points.partial_credit: Half if it says a classifier works better or more easily after the transform but does not say simple/linear classifiers can handle complex data.

rubric.notes: Full marks (2) for both ideas: nonlinear features capture complex patterns/make classes separable, and simple classifiers like SVM can then classify complex data well. Give part marks for a vague or half-stated version of either idea. Give none for wrong or unrelated statements such as dimensionality reduction or normalization only; each point is marked independently and different wording is fine.
